title: Once sampling error and heterogeneity are subtracted, does error in predicting later trials grow with calendar gap?
question: In repeated older-to-newer holdouts on real networks, does standardized prediction error grow with the calendar gap to the training evidence beyond what sampling error and ordinary heterogeneity explain, and does the raw error slope mistake those components for drift?
design: Five aggregate networks with publication years from multinma, netmeta and metadat; random-effects NMA fitted to every trial published at least 0, 3, 6, 10 or 15 years before each held-out trial; slope of the standardized squared error on gap against each network's own simulated no-drift null. 5 networks, 400 null and 200 drift replicates each.
